papers.title: OmniPersist: Persistent Dynamic World Modeling via Coupled Panoramic Evolution
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models play a vital role in robotics and autonomous driving, yet existing video diffusion models struggle to maintain dynamic object persistence. When the camera turns away and returns, out-of-view moving entities fail to evolve plausibly in latent space, often mutating or vanishing entirely due to bounded perspective views. To resolve this issue, we propose OmniPersist, a unified framework that couples perspective video generation with panoramic evolution within a single-stage diffusion model, without relying on auxiliary models or initial panoramic inputs. To maintain efficiency, we model the panoramic stream at a lower frame rate, bridging both views across space and time via Geometric Anchoring (GeoAnch) for spatial correspondence and Temporal Compensation (TemComp) for temporal aggregation. OmniPersist is agnostic to camera-control architectures, supporting both latent-level and attention-level conditioning. Extensive experiments on a newly constructed dynamic benchmark across image-to-video and video continuation tasks demonstrate consistent gains in visual quality, camera controllability, revisit consistency, and dynamic persistence.
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对摄像机转离后再返回时，世界模型中的动态物体容易突变、消失或运动不连续的问题，提出 OmniPersist。该方法在共享的视频扩散模型中联合生成高帧率透视视频和低帧率全景视频，使全景空间持续记录视野外实体的运动状态；GeoAnch 负责同步时刻的跨视图几何特征对齐，TemComp 负责利用邻近时间的特征弥补全景流的时间稀疏。方法无需辅助模型或初始全景输入，并可兼容 CameraCtrl 和 UCPE 两类摄像机控制方式。基于约12.5万个训练片段和300个评测片段的实验显示，该方法在视觉质量、摄像机控制、背景重访保真度以及动态主体身份、可见性和轨迹保持方面持续优于对应基线，同时通过稀疏全景采样控制了计算开销。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 OmniPersist 单阶段统一框架，在透视视频生成的同时以时间稀疏方式演化360度全景状态，以维持视野外动态主体的持续性。2. 提出 GeoAnch，通过显式几何对应在同步时刻交换透视视图和全景视图特征；提出 TemComp，通过邻近时间聚合弥补两种流之间的帧率差异。3. 构建配对的全景—透视动态数据集，覆盖目标跟踪、单次重访、双重重访和近360度旋转等摄像机轨迹。4. 在图像到视频和视频续生成任务中，基于潜在层级和注意力层级两种摄像机控制机制验证了动态持续性、重访一致性及整体生成质量的提升。
papers.relevance_cn: 与研究重点高度相关。该工作直接面向动作条件视觉世界模型和闭环模拟中的状态持久化问题，使用全景演化为视野外动态实体提供持续的空间记忆。其共享扩散Transformer、跨视图几何对齐和跨时间特征聚合机制与视频扩散、长视频一致性及缓存复用密切相关；低帧率全景流在保持动态状态的同时降低了计算量，体现了稀疏计算和效率优化。不过，论文主要验证离线的图像到视频与视频续生成，并未实现实时闭环交互。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，OmniPersist 的训练依赖全景视频数据，因而需要相应的全景数据资源。作者还将实时流式生成、长时域视频生成以及机器人导航列为未来工作，说明这些能力尚未在本文中解决。此外，实验数据集由全景视频渲染出透视轨迹，评测规模为300个视频；论文未明确说明在真实机器人传感器、在线动作反馈或更长时间跨度下的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_cn: 动作条件世界模型在机器人和自动驾驶中发挥着重要作用，但现有视频扩散模型难以维持动态物体的持续存在。当摄像机转开后再次返回时，视野外移动实体无法在潜在空间中合理演化，常常由于视角范围受限而发生突变或完全消失。为解决这一问题，我们提出 OmniPersist：一种统一框架，在单阶段扩散模型中将透视视频生成与全景演化耦合起来，无需辅助模型或初始全景输入。为保持效率，我们以更低的帧率建模全景流，并通过几何锚定（GeoAnch）实现空间对应、通过时间补偿（TemComp）实现时间聚合，从而在空间和时间上连接两种视图。OmniPersist 不依赖特定的摄像机控制架构，既支持潜在层级条件控制，也支持注意力层级条件控制。在新构建的动态基准上针对图像到视频和视频续生成任务进行的大量实验表明，该方法在视觉质量、摄像机可控性、重访一致性和动态持续性方面均取得稳定提升。

papers.title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation
papers.abstract: Video-to-audio generation synthesizes sound that matches a video in content and timing, with applications ranging from film post-production to live streaming, games and interactive world models. Interactive applications receive video continuously and need the sound to follow it in real time, yet most existing video-to-audio models are bidirectional and must observe an entire clip before producing any sound. We propose LiveAudio, a streaming video-to-audio framework that generates high-quality and synchronized audio in real time while the video is playing. In contrast to prior streaming models trained from scratch, LiveAudio converts a bidirectional model into a streaming generator so as to build on its audio quality and synchronization. LiveAudio generates audio block by block, and each block depends only on the video that has already been played. The streaming generator is obtained from the bidirectional model through progressive causal fine-tuning and distillation, so that each block needs only a few sampling steps. Experiments on VGGSound show that LiveAudio outperforms existing streaming models in audio quality and synchronization, and surpasses the bidirectional model it starts from in synchronization. On a single A100 GPU, it runs in real time with a real-time factor of 0.79 and a time to first frame of 143 ms. Audio samples are available at https://streamaudio.github.io.
papers.summary_cn: LiveAudio 将离线双向视频到音频扩散模型转换为因果、自回归、实时流式生成器。模型采用因果音频 VAE、块因果 DiT、无前视的同步对齐视频条件和块级 KV 缓存，按块生成并立即播放音频。训练分为双向预训练、块因果微调、ODE 少步蒸馏和非对称 DMD 四个阶段，其中 DMD 使用双向教师恢复因果化造成的同步损失。VGGSound 实验显示，LiveAudio 在流式模型中具有更好的音频质量和同步性，并在同步性上优于所用双向教师；单张 A100 上首帧延迟为 143 毫秒、实时因子为 0.79，同时支持流式视频文本到音频和文本到音频生成。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 LiveAudio，将双向视频到音频模型转换为自回归扩散流式生成器，而不是从头训练流式模型。2. 提出从双向模型到实时生成器的渐进式训练流程，依次进行因果化、ODE 少步蒸馏和非对称 DMD。3. 通过同步对齐视频条件、块因果 DiT、因果音频 VAE 和 KV 缓存，实现仅依赖已播放视频的低延迟块级生成。4. 证明非对称 DMD 可以恢复因果建模造成的音视频同步损失，并使同步性超过双向教师。5. 在 VGGSound 上取得优于现有流式模型的音频质量和同步结果，并验证了流式视频文本到音频及文本到音频能力。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作与实时生成、流式生成、因果扩散、长视频生成和缓存复用高度相关。它将双向扩散模型离线到在线转换为块级自回归生成器，使每个音频块只使用已经到达的视频，避免未来帧信息泄漏；通过四步无 CFG 的 ODE 蒸馏降低采样成本，通过块因果注意力和 KV cache 避免重复计算历史上下文。其面向直播、游戏和交互式世界模型的实时音频伴随生成，展示了闭环或持续输入场景中低延迟多模态生成的实现路径。它主要生成视频对应的音频，而不是生成视频本身，因此与视频扩散模型的关系主要体现在因果化、蒸馏、流式推理和缓存机制的可迁移设计上。
papers.limitations_cn: 实验主要基于 VGGSound 测试集，训练使用 10 秒视频片段；论文仅报告了有限数据集和场景下的结果，对更长时长、复杂场景及分布外视频的泛化能力未充分验证。模型约有 12 亿参数，实时性是在单张 NVIDIA A100、批大小为 1 的条件下测得，普通硬件或更高分辨率输入下的性能未明确说明。因果约束会造成音频质量和同步性下降，虽然非对称 DMD 能够缓解这一问题，但其使用双向教师和自生成历史，训练过程较复杂且存在质量与分布匹配之间的权衡。论文未明确说明在持续运行很长时间时误差累积、缓存增长、异常输入恢复以及端到端交互闭环中的稳定性。
papers.abstract_cn: 视频到音频生成旨在合成在内容和时间上与视频匹配的声音，应用范围从电影后期制作到直播、游戏和交互式世界模型。交互式应用会持续接收视频，并需要声音实时跟随视频；然而，大多数现有视频到音频模型是双向的，必须观察完整视频片段后才能产生声音。我们提出 LiveAudio，一种流式视频到音频框架，可在视频播放的同时实时生成高质量且同步的音频。不同于从头训练的以往流式模型，LiveAudio 将双向模型转换为流式生成器，从而继承其音频质量和同步能力。LiveAudio 逐块生成音频，每个音频块仅依赖已经播放的视频。该流式生成器通过渐进式因果微调和蒸馏从双向模型获得，因此每个音频块只需少量采样步骤。在 VGGSound 上的实验表明，LiveAudio 在音频质量和同步性方面优于现有流式模型，并且在同步性上超过了作为其起点的双向模型。在单张 A100 GPU 上，它能够实时运行，实时因子为 0.79，首帧时间为 143 毫秒。音频样例见 https://streamaudio.github.io。

papers.title: A Mesh to Remember: Persistent Appearance for Interactive Video Worlds
papers.abstract: Video world models synthesize photorealistic observations in response to user actions but struggle to remain consistent over long interactions. Coding agents and text-to-3D models instead generate explicit 3D worlds whose geometry and state persist by construction, but whose appearance falls far short of photorealism. Recent methods combine the strengths of both by rendering such worlds into coarse proxies that guide a video model. However, since these proxies only specify where things are, the renderer must invent what they look like as the world is explored, and anything it forgets is reinvented when a surface reappears. Our key insight is that a mesh identifies which surface each pixel shows, across frames and views, even as objects move, allowing it to serve as an address for what the renderer generates. We propose M2R (Mesh to Remember), a few-step causal video renderer that stores its own features on the surfaces they depict, in each object's frame, and retrieves them by rasterizing the mesh whenever those surfaces come back into view. Appearance thus travels with objects wherever they move, persists across revisits, and is shared by every agent that observes it, while memory grows with the surfaces seen instead of the number of frames. Trained only on synthetic data, M2R transfers zero-shot to real indoor scans and to worlds authored by coding agents. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods in consistency across static, dynamic, and multi-agent benchmarks, more than doubling object permanence and nearly doubling cross-agent consistency, while rendering 720p video in real time (40 FPS).
papers.summary_cn: Video world models synthesize photorealistic observations in response to user actions but struggle to remain consistent over long interactions.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose M2R (Mesh to Remember), a few-step causal video renderer that stores its own features on the surfaces they depict, in each object's frame, and retrieves them by rasterizing the mesh whenever those surfaces come back into view.

papers.title: DraftKV: Protecting Persistent Worlds through Hierarchical Streaming Retrieval
papers.abstract: Interactive video world models enable action- and camera-controlled exploration, yet struggle to maintain consistent spatial geometry and appearance when revisiting previously explored locations. Historical KV caches help auto-regressive video diffusion models maintain long-term consistency, but their retrieval and attention computation introduce substantial latency as history grows. We propose DraftKV, a training-free framework that retrieves historical KV caches based on geometric grounding and query-conditioned relevance, while combining CPU offloading with tile-wise streaming attention to reduce GPU memory usage and inference latency. Theoretically, we show that draft relevance reproduces the mean branch of full-resolution block relevance exactly, so its deviation is confined to the $β$-weighted max branch, and we bound retrieval utility loss in terms of the measured Top-K selection overlap. We further show that draft relevance cannot distinguish blocks with similar pooled descriptors regardless of camera pose, motivating geometric grounding before refinement. Then, we introduce streaming CG-Attention, which overlaps CPU-to-GPU KV transfers with attention computation through tile-wise streaming, hiding transfer latency while maintaining bounded GPU memory usage. Experiments across diverse model families show that DraftKV achieves superior generation quality and consistency while achieving $3.27\times$ end-to-end speedup and 42.2% peak GPU memory reduction over other CPU-offloaded KV cache retrieval methods. Notably, DraftKV enables high-quality interactive world generation with historical KV retrieval on a single H100 GPU using SolarWM-33B.

papers.contribution_cn: We propose DraftKV, a training-free framework that retrieves historical KV caches based on geometric grounding and query-conditioned relevance, while combining CPU offloading with tile-wise streaming attention to reduce GPU memory usage and inference latency.

papers.title: On-Policy Codec Distillation for Efficient All-in-One Video Generation
papers.abstract: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence. Consequently, conditioning quickly dominates the computation cost. Yet most of these tokens carry redundant spatiotemporal information. Our key insight is that identifying what is genuinely new is exactly the problem that classical video codecs have long solved. Thus, we first introduce a codec-based token pruning method that discards redundant tokens. Then, we propose an on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) strategy to train a DiT adapter capable of learning the codec pruning pattern well without quality degradation. Together, they form On-Policy Codec Distillation (CodecOPSD). We scale CodecOPSD to 16 condition modalities on our own video diffusion model, where it prunes 66% of the condition tokens on average with almost no quality drop. Therefore, denoising becomes 2x faster, and the cache memory shrinks by up to 73% in KV cache mode. CodecOPSD also extends to other state-of-the-art pretrained image and video generative models, where its benefit grows further with more conditions, longer frames, and higher resolution.
papers.summary_cn: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence.
papers.contribution_cn: Then, we propose an on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) strategy to train a DiT adapter capable of learning the codec pruning pattern well without quality degradation.

papers.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Specifically, RG denoises the re-noised previous chunk once under the new prompt without the cache and adds the resulting residual to the early denoising steps of the next chunk, where its content is largely decided and the new prompt is most suppressed. Across settings ranging from a single switch to long multi-switch generation, RG substantially improves prompt switching capability on existing streaming models, including those with dedicated switching mechanisms, while largely retaining visual quality. As it requires no training or per-model tuning and adds only one forward pass per chunk, RG can be easily integrated into existing real-time video generation pipelines.
papers.summary_cn: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video.
papers.contribution_cn: Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache.

papers.title: DiffGR00T: Execution-Aware Differentiable Training for Humanoid Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong results in arm-centric manipulation, yet humanoid whole-body control (WBC) requires dynamic balance and tightly coupled full-body coordination. Existing hierarchical humanoid VLAs typically decouple motion generation from physical execution, leaving tracking and balance errors unable to directly optimize the VLA generator. We propose DiffGR00T, an end-to-end differentiable training framework that couples GR00T N1.7 with SONIC, a pretrained whole-body behavior foundation model. To enable execution-aware differentiable training, we replace the non-differentiable simulator with a learned, action-conditioned world model, allowing multi-step body-execution losses to backpropagate through the frozen whole-body controller and the flow-matching sampler directly into the VLA action head. On four HumanoidArena simulation tasks, DiffGR00T improves average task success by 12.5 percentage points over the supervised base VLA (59.2% to 71.7%), demonstrating that execution-aware gradients effectively align high-level motion generation with closed-loop whole-body dynamics.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Conference preprint. Corresponding author: Hesheng Wang

papers.title: Analyzing and Improving FlowMap Distillation of Autoregressive Video Models
papers.abstract: FlowMap distillation offers a natural route to few-step generative modeling by directly learning a teacher's denoising trajectories. Yet for autoregressive (AR) video generation, existing few-step models still rely on distribution matching distillation (DMD) to remain competitive, sacrificing sample diversity and requiring a large bidirectional teacher. In this work, we analyze what limits standalone AR FlowMap distillation and introduce two complementary guidance mechanisms to close this gap: (1) anti-drifting guidance, which helps the AR teacher correct drifted student rollouts by training an auxiliary model to mimic student drift and using it as a negative guidance branch; and (2) motion-aware guidance, which makes motion easier for a FlowMap student to learn by locating motion patches and selectively applying skip-layer guidance. Empirically, our approach applies to $π$-Flow, MeanFlow, and consistency distillation with 1.3B AR teachers, improving generation quality and reducing drift over 30 s rollouts. Notably, our 4-step $π$-Flow students match DMD students distilled from 14B teachers on VBench while preserving the sample diversity of their AR teachers, demonstrating that pure FlowMap distillation is effective for few-step autoregressive video generation.
papers.summary_cn: FlowMap distillation offers a natural route to few-step generative modeling by directly learning a teacher's denoising trajectories.

papers.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning. Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretraining stage. Our key insight is that visual prediction encourages control-relevant features, while value supervision promotes task-relevant representations; together, they shape a representation suited to policy learning. Built on an image-editing backbone, DexWAC predicts, for each action chunk, the visual latent and proprioception at its endpoint together with its reward and continuation, so the world model alone efficiently yields complete imagined transitions without generating intermediate video frames. After adapting the world model and critic on real rollouts, we improve the pretrained actor through either PPO on imagined rollouts or critic-guided best-of-$N$ selection. DexWAC surpasses the large-scale pretrained VLA and WAM baselines in simulation and achieves 75% average success on two real-world tasks, compared with 45% for $π_{0.5}$. Its world model is more accurate and faster than video-based baselines, and ablations confirm that learning dynamics and value together improves the policy.
papers.summary_cn: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretraining stage.

papers.title: Interactive Neural Computers
papers.abstract: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability. We explore an overlooked alternative. Rather than training an agent to operate an existing computer, we train a generative model to be the computer, predicting each next screen from past screens and the user's mouse and keyboard actions. Treating a desktop as an interactive world model raises problems that natural-video world models largely avoid. Without a camera pose to index memory, the model must remember content that has left the screen without any geometric cues. Arithmetic in a terminal has to be exactly right, not merely plausible. Small interface text must also stay legible at interactive frame rates. Our Interactive Neural Computer is structured like a Neural Turing Machine and starts to address these problems with three modules trained end to end from pixels and actions. A surprise-gated slot memory, supervised by latent next-frame prediction (MEMORY-JEPA), stores what is off screen. An exploratory query bridge brings in the reasoning of a pretrained VLM, and a residual renderer predicts only the latent changes between frames. In long closed-loop rollouts, our model recalls occluded files in 64.2% of trials (chance is 33.3%), compared with at most 56.0% for recurrent and sliding-window baselines. It also raises terminal-text OCR accuracy from 1.3% to 50.1%. Finally, because the memory is explicit, it can be transplanted at test time to causally change what the model renders.
papers.summary_cn: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents.
